ORDER
During the pendency of the captioned appeals before the Board
of Land Appeals, the parties noted above petitioned the United States
District Court for the District of Colorado for declaratory and
injunctive relief the requirements for compliance with 43
2802.1-2, pertaining to of costs to the Government for
for processing right-of-way The Board informed these
parties and others similarly situated that it would withhold consid
eration of their appeals pending the outcome of the federal court
litigation.
On May 31, 1977, the District Court issued its Memorandum Opin
ion and Order granting the motion for summary judgment by the
plaintiff parties. Civil Action No. 76-F-48, 433 F. Supp. 144. The
Department was required to consider the subject cases in accordance
with the standards given in the court's order.
77-1734 and 77-1735, were filed with the United States Court of
Appeals for the Tenth Circuit, but were dismissed on 22,
1977, upon stipulation of the United States and the other parties.
The Bureau of Land Management on February 2, 1978, filed with
this Board a motion for remand of the captioned appeals in order that
it might comply with the mandate of the district court. We are

75-580, 76-317 and 77-161
remanding the captioned to the Director of the Bureau of Land
since the Bureau of Land Management is the proper
Departmental office for initial action in complying with the District
order.
The Bureau of Land Management's motion does not refer to Southern
California Edison's appeals in IBLA 76-317 and Upon that
request, by order of February 28, 1977, we consolidated these
appeals with IBLA 75-580 since they involve the same right-of-way
applications and present identical issues and statements of reasons.
these reasons, and for the purpose of administrative clarity, we
are remanding to the BLM herewith on our own motion Southern California
Edison's appeals in 76-317 and IBLA 77-161.
Therefore, pursuant to the authority delegated to the Board of
Land Appeals by the Secretary of the Interior, 43 4.1, the
captioned decisions appealed from are set aside and the cases are
remanded to the Director, Bureau of Land Management for appropriate
action consistent with the court's decision.
